newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros secessionists boycott independence day.
newsitem.headline: Comoros secessionists boycott independence day.

text.p: French flags flew in protest over Anjouan, largest island in the Comoros, where most islanders boycotted low-key celebrations marking 22 years of independence on Sunday, residents reported.

The flags, and the flag of a 19th-century sultanate, were hoisted by supporters of a secessionist movement who want Anjouan to return to France. They say independence has brought only poverty and political unrest to the Indian Ocean islands.
On the main island of Grand Comore, the anniversary celebrations began shortly after president Mohamed Taki arrived back from a visit to France.
Taki's arrival in a private jet angered local civil servants, still waiting for their June salaries to be paid, who said the poverty-stricken republic could not afford such a luxury.

On Anjouan, local youths booed the security forces and local officials at the brief independence flag-raising ceremony, while other islanders said they were observing a day of mourning. No violence was reported.
Many foreigners who normally live on Anjouan crossed to Grand Comore for the weekend, fearing unrest on Independence Day.
The main group of islands declared themselves independent of France in 1975. But Mayotte island, within sight of Anjouan, chose to remain French and is not part of the Comoros Republic.
